title: Consistent embedding normalization for multi-model reranker and legacy client compatibility
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Summary:
We observed inconsistent reranker scores when combining embeddings produced by different model families (older dense models vs newer quantized models). The root cause is inconsistent normalization and ambiguity about the intended distance metric (cosine vs dot) across clients and server-side adapters. Some clients rely on raw dot-product units, others expect cosine similarity, and a subset send pre-normalized vectors. This ticket aims to: (1) enforce a canonical server-side normalization policy for reranker scoring; (2) add a compatibility shim allowing legacy clients to opt into previous behavior; (3) provide runtime telemetry and clear client migration guidance.

Problem details:
- Cross-model score drift: reranker A/B experiments show >6% drop in NDCG when mixing older models with new family after an upstream tokenization/float16 change.
- Incoming vectors have mixed norms: some generator clients normalize, others don't; some models produce lower-norm embeddings due to quantization scale differences.
- Ambiguous metric: product codebase includes both cosine and dot scoring paths; default behavior depends on the model adapter and has drifted.

Proposed plan:
1) Server canonicalization: always compute scores using a documented pipeline: ensure embeddings are L2-normalized server-side and use cosine similarity by default for rerank endpoint. This preserves unit interpretability and is robust to embedding magnitude differences.
2) Backcompat "compat-mode" header: introduce X-Redwood-Embed-Scoring: {"mode":"legacy-dot"|"cosine"|"auto-detect"} (clients can set to preserve prior behavior). If header absent, default to "cosine". For "auto-detect", the runtime will run a fast norm heuristic (if mean ||v|| falls below threshold, assume pre-normalized input and skip server normalization).
3) Runtime safeguard: add a validation step that logs anomalous norm distributions and rejects extreme outliers with 400 + explanatory error to avoid silent quality regressions.
4) Rollout and metrics: enable feature flag for a small % of traffic, capture NDCG, latency, token-cost delta, distribution of incoming norms, and percent of requests using compat header.
5) Migration docs: publish step-by-step guide for client teams showing how to opt-in to server normalization, how to compute cosine locally if desired, and how to compare scores to previous baseline.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit + integration tests cover scoring paths (cosine, dot, pre-normalized inputs).
- No more than 5% regression in NDCG on the mixed-model rerank benchmark when defaulting to server-side cosine vs current production baseline.
- Telemetry dashboard shows norm distribution and percent-compat header usage.
- Feature flag allows safe rollback without data loss.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Normalizing server-side adds ~0.12ms per request at median when implemented efficiently with a fused L2 kernel; we should measure and optimize in the runtime.
- Choosing cosine as default helps stability across open models but may change unit semantics for downstream scoring thresholds; hence the compat header and rollout.
- Auto-detect heuristics will be conservative to avoid false assumptions; logs will be sampled for manual review.

Testing / QA:
- Synthetic test suite combining embeddings from three model families (legacy-v1, quant-v2, open-large) and comparing rerank order with and without normalization.
- Canary rollout to 5% traffic with canary flag and monitoring alerts on NDCG / latency / error rate.
- End-to-end test with client SDKs to validate header behavior and error messages.

Links / artifacts:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Embed+Normalization+Design
- Benchmark dashboard (internal): https://dash.redwood.ai/rerank/embed-normalization
- PR (runtime): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1482
- PR (rerank-api shim): https://github.com/redwood-inference/api/pull/622

Open questions:
- Thresholds for auto-detect: initial suggestion mean_norm < 1.05 -> "pre-normalized". Need validation on corpora.
- Should we expose a per-account setting (enterprise) that pins legacy-dot for a longer window? Proposal: yes; add to Dedicated feature backlog.

Next steps:
- Implement fused L2-normalize kernel (ENG infra spike, 2d) -> assign Eng infra pair.
- Add compat header parsing and header unit tests.
- Create canary flag and wire telemetry.
- Draft client migration guide and notify SDK teams.
